Fix a four-dimensional smooth spacetime region $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with a stated orientation, spin structure, boundary conditions, and unit system. A selected model specifies a continuous global symmetry group $H$, its action on the fields and observables, the nondynamical background connections, the field and jet domains, a regulator and measure or formal perturbative generating functional, and the admissible local counterterms. A background connection is nondynamical model data: it transforms under local changes of background trivialization but is not integrated over.

Let $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{g,p}$ be the finite-jet horizontal $p$-forms of ghost number $g$ generated by the nondynamical background connections and their BRST ghost jets, without matter-field jets, and restrict the model’s nilpotent BRST differential $s$ and horizontal exterior derivative $d_H$ to this background subalgebra. An infinitesimal local anomaly representative is a local horizontal four-form $a_4\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{1,4}$ such that $sa_4+d_Hb_3=0$ for some $b_3\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{2,3}$. The **local perturbative ’t Hooft anomaly** of the specified global symmetry is the class $[a_4]$ in the relative cohomology $H^{1,4}(s\mid d_H)$ of this background subalgebra, with the quotient taken using exactly the model’s admissible four-dimensional background counterterms and total-derivative boundary convention. Its class is zero exactly when an admissible local counterterm removes the infinitesimal background variation modulo a boundary term.

Any prescribed noninvariance of the classical action or selected couplings is an explicit-symmetry-breaking insertion and is separated before assigning this quantum anomaly class. It is not, by itself, a measure anomaly. A claim of anomaly matching therefore assumes the stated classical symmetry, or carries such breaking insertions separately.

This definition applies to a global symmetry whose background is nondynamical. If the same local class concerns a field integrated over as a gauge redundancy, it is a local gauge anomaly, not a ’t Hooft anomaly; an uncancelled gauge anomaly obstructs the proposed gauging unless a separately specified cancellation mechanism is included. The definition addresses only infinitesimal transformations and makes no claim about large or disconnected transformations, determinant-line holonomy, torsion phases, or a physical continuum limit.

Fix an even integer $d\ge2$, a compact smooth oriented Riemannian $d$-manifold $M$ without boundary with a specified spin structure, a smooth principal right $G$-bundle $P\to M$ with connection $A$, and a unitary finite-dimensional complex representation $R:G\to U(V_R)$. Let $E_R=P\times_R V_R$ be the associated Hermitian bundle. Let $S^+$ and $S^-$ be the associated bundles of the two half-spin representations of $\operatorname{Spin}(d)$. The chiral Dirac operator is the first-order operator

$$D^+_{A,R}:H^1(M;S^+\otimes E_R)\longrightarrow L^2(M;S^-\otimes E_R),$$

where $H^1$ and $L^2$ are the first Sobolev and square-integrable completions for the fixed Riemannian metric. Assume the operator is Fredholm. Its inverse determinant line is

$$\mathcal L_A=\left(\det_{\mathbb C}\ker D^+_{A,R}\right)^*\otimes\det_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{coker}D^+_{A,R},$$

with $\det_{\mathbb C}W=\bigwedge^{\dim_{\mathbb C}W}_{\mathbb C}W$. For a smooth family of such Fredholm operators over a parameter manifold, use the Quillen metric and the Bismut–Freed unitary connection on this line bundle. For a real or pseudoreal fermionic quadratic form, the Pfaffian line replaces the determinant line and carries its induced Hermitian metric and unitary connection.

Let $\mathcal A(P)$ be the affine space of smooth connections on $P$, and let $\mathcal G(P)$ be the group of smooth bundle automorphisms covering the identity on $M$. A gauge arrow $u:A\to A^u$ induces a unitary map $u_*:\mathcal L_A\to\mathcal L_{A^u}$ by its action on kernel and cokernel. A closed loop in background/gauge-field space consists of a smooth path $A_t$ in $\mathcal A(P)$, $0\le t\le1$, and an endpoint gauge arrow $u:A_0\to A_1$. Let $\mathrm{PT}_{A_t}:\mathcal L_{A_0}\to\mathcal L_{A_1}$ be parallel transport and $u_*:\mathcal L_{A_0}\to\mathcal L_{A_1}$ the endpoint gauge map. The closed-loop automorphism is $u_*^{-1}\circ\mathrm{PT}_{A_t}$ on $\mathcal L_{A_0}$. Its scalar is the holonomy $\operatorname{Hol}_{\gamma}(\mathcal L)\in U(1)$. Fix the regularization and local-counterterm convention before comparing this loop phase with the infinitesimal local anomaly; the holonomy itself is additional global loop data.

Fix an integer $d\ge1$. Let $Y$ be a compact oriented smooth spin $(d+1)$-manifold with boundary $M=\partial Y$, using the outward-normal-first boundary orientation. A background $b$ consists of the metric, spin structure, and any specified principal-bundle connections and associated fields on $Y$; its restriction to $M$ is the boundary background. A $d$-dimensional boundary theory is **relative to an invertible bulk theory** when its partition value is a vector $Z_\partial(M,b|_M)$ in a specified one-dimensional Hermitian line $\mathcal L_\partial(M,b|_M)$, and the bulk assigns the dual line $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk}}(M,b|_M)\cong\mathcal L_\partial(M,b|_M)^*$ together with a vector $Z_{\mathrm{bulk}}(Y,b)$ in that line. The canonical evaluation

$$\mathrm{ev}:\mathcal L_\partial(M,b|_M)\otimes\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk}}(M,b|_M)\longrightarrow\mathbb C$$

then defines the combined scalar amplitude. Invertibility means that the bulk assigns a one-dimensional line to each closed $d$-dimensional boundary background and an isomorphism to each bordism map; orientation reversal replaces the assigned line by its dual. For a loop $\gamma$ of compatible background fields and endpoint gauge identifications, the boundary/bulk pair cancels that anomaly along $\gamma$ exactly when

$$\operatorname{Hol}_{\gamma}(\mathcal L_\partial)\operatorname{Hol}_{\gamma}(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk}})=1.$$

The diagram records this condition: the vertical maps are the line evaluation at the two endpoints, and the top map is parallel transport on both lines.

~~~tikzcd
\mathcal L_{\partial,0}\otimes\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk},0}
  \arrow[r,"\mathrm{PT}^{\partial}_{\gamma}\otimes\mathrm{PT}^{\mathrm{bulk}}_{\gamma}"]
  \arrow[d,"\mathrm{ev}_0"'] &
\mathcal L_{\partial,1}\otimes\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk},1}
  \arrow[d,"\mathrm{ev}_1"] \\
\mathbb C \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}_{\mathbb C}"'] & \mathbb C
~~~

A **finite groupoid** is a small category in which every morphism is invertible, with finitely many isomorphism classes and a finite automorphism group at every object. Write $\pi_0(\mathcal C)$ for its set of isomorphism classes. Its **groupoid cardinality** is

$$|\mathcal C|:=\sum_{[c]\in\pi_0(\mathcal C)}\frac{1}{|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal C}(c)|}.$$

For an isomorphism-invariant function $f:\pi_0(\mathcal C)\to\mathbb C$, define

$$\int_{c\in\mathcal C} f(c):=\sum_{[c]\in\pi_0(\mathcal C)}\frac{f(c)}{|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal C}(c)|}.$$

For finite groupoids $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$, a functor $p:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, and an object $d$ of $\mathcal D$, its **homotopy fiber** $\mathcal C_d$ has objects $(c,\alpha)$ with $\alpha:p(c)\overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow}d$ and morphisms $u:(c,\alpha)\to(c',\alpha')$ satisfying $\alpha'\circ p(u)=\alpha$. Define pullback and pushforward of invariant functions by

$$(p^*g)([c])=g([p(c)]),\qquad (p_!f)([d])=\int_{(c,\alpha)\in\mathcal C_d} f([c]).$$

A span $\mathcal X\xleftarrow{a}\mathcal E\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal Y$ of finite groupoids therefore induces the linear map $b_!a^*$ on invariant functions.

Assume full AC. Give the unit sphere $S^4\subset\mathbb R^5$ its boundary orientation, round metric and standard spin structure induced from the Euclidean ball. Let $S=S^+\oplus S^-$ be its complex spinor bundle, with skew-Hermitian Clifford action $c(v)c(w)+c(w)c(v)=-2\langle v,w\rangle$ and positive chirality the $+1$ eigenspace of $\Gamma=-c(e_1)c(e_2)c(e_3)c(e_4)$ in an oriented orthonormal frame. A spin lift here is a principal $\operatorname{Spin}(4)$ bundle double-covering the oriented orthonormal frame bundle; explicitly $\operatorname{Spin}(4)=Sp(1)\times Sp(1)$ covers $SO(4)$ by $(a,b):q\mapsto aqb^{-1}$ on $\mathbb H\cong\mathbb R^4$, where $Sp(1)$ is the unit-quaternion group, identified with $SU(2)$. The connection on spinors is the lift of the Levi-Civita connection. Set $E=S^+$ with its rank-two Hermitian $SU(2)$ connection $A_+$.

The twisted chiral Dirac operator $D^+_{A_+}=\sum_i c(e_i)\nabla_{e_i}:H^1(S^4;S^+\otimes E)\to L^2(S^4;S^-\otimes E)$ is Fredholm, with complex kernel dimension $1$, cokernel dimension $0$ and index $1$. In the anti-Hermitian Chern convention,

$$
\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle=\frac1{8\pi^2}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}(F_{A_+}\wedge F_{A_+})=-1.
$$

Its positive trace-form instanton charge $q=-(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int\operatorname{tr}(F\wedge F)$ is $1$; its connection is the scale-one self-dual BPST connection. More precisely there are parallel unitary identifications $F:\Lambda^0_{\mathbb C}\oplus\Lambda^2_{+,\mathbb C}\to S^+\otimes S^+$ and $G:\Lambda^1_{\mathbb C}\to S^-\otimes S^+$ under which

$$
G^{-1}D^+_{A_+}F(f,\omega)=df+\sqrt2\,d^*\omega.
$$

Here $\Lambda^2_+$ is the $+1$ Hodge-star subbundle, $d^*$ is the Riemannian formal adjoint, and all Sobolev spaces and adjoints use the specified bundle metrics. In the complete twisted spinor bundle the full Dirac operator is selfadjoint with domain $H^1$ and its square has domain $H^2$. This is a direct operator calculation for this explicit bundle, not an application of a general index formula.

Assume full AC and use the explicit round spin sphere, $E=S^+$ connection, Clifford action and chiral Dirac operator of the round-sphere spin-twist lemma. Let $Y=S^4\times(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)$ have product metric, pulled-back gauge connection and periodic, nonbounding circle spin structure. On the pulled-back complex bundle $S\otimes E$, put $c_5=i\Gamma$ and $D_5=D_4+i\Gamma\partial_t$, with periodic Sobolev domain $H^1$. There is a parallel antiunitary involution $J$ preserving $\ker D_5$, and the real skew-adjoint realization $iD_5$ on its $J$-fixed Hilbert space has

$$
\dim_{\mathbb R}(\ker D_5)^J=\dim_{\mathbb C}\ker D_4=1, \qquad \operatorname{ind}_2(iD_5):=\dim_{\mathbb R}(\ker D_5)^J\bmod2=1.
$$

More generally, let a nonempty compact closed oriented Riemannian spin four-manifold have a smooth unitary $SU(2)$ rank-two twist and a Fredholm chiral Dirac realization with $n_+=\dim_{\mathbb C}\ker D^+$ and $n_-=\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{coker}D^+$. With the same Clifford and periodic product conventions, the real product kernel has dimension $n_++n_-$, its parity is $\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb C}D^+\bmod2$, and the central action on its inverse determinant line is $(-1)^{\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb C}D^+}$. This general product statement does not assign an index value to an arbitrary bundle.

Let $z=-I$ be the central gauge automorphism of $E$. On the inverse chiral determinant line

$$
\mathcal L=(\det_{\mathbb C}\ker D^+)^*\otimes\det_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{coker}D^+
$$

its induced action is $-1$. For the constant connection path closed by $z$, the closed-loop automorphism $z_*^{-1}\circ\mathrm{PT}$ is $-1$ for any supplied connection on the determinant line. The $N$-fold tensor power has action $(-1)^N$.

The spin convention is part of the statement: using antiperiodic spinors in the circle direction gives no product zero mode. Equivalently, gluing the gauge fibers by $z=-1$ with an antiperiodic spin clutch gives periodic total spinor boundary conditions; gluing by $z$ with periodic spin clutch gives antiperiodic total boundary conditions instead. This distinguishes the tested fermion-parity mapping-torus convention from an automatic eta-holonomy formula. No general spectral-flow or Atiyah–Singer theorem is asserted.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

citations.quote: Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Let $M=S^4$ with its boundary orientation, a specified smooth Riemannian metric and standard spin structure, and let $E\to M$ be a smooth rank-two Hermitian bundle with structure group $SU(2)$ and smooth unitary connection $A$. Treat $SU(2)$ as a nondynamical background global symmetry and consider one massless left-handed Weyl fermion in the fundamental representation. Use the inverse determinant/Pfaffian line and the index-density normalization $I_6=[\widehat A(TM)\operatorname{ch}(E)]_6$ for its universal local anomaly polynomial, with $F_A$ anti-Hermitian and $\operatorname{ch}(E)=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf 2}\exp(-F_A/(2\pi i))$. Assume the selected background is in the index-one sector, meaning the coupled chiral Dirac operator $D_A^+$ is Fredholm and $\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb C}D_A^+=1$. For a proved concrete instance, assume full AC and take the unit round metric, $E=S^+$ and the positive-spin Levi-Civita connection: its complex chiral kernel has dimension $1$, its cokernel dimension $0$, and $\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle=-1$ in the convention $c(E)=\det(I-F_A/(2\pi i))$. The conditional conclusion below still applies to every stipulated index-one background; this concrete instance supplies that index by proof rather than as a physical postulate. Let $z=-I\in SU(2)$ act on the fermion fibers and form the corresponding order-two loop $\gamma_z$ of the background/gauge-field groupoid. Since $z$ acts as $-1$ in the fundamental representation, its action on this fermion is the same twist as $(-1)^F$; use the fermion-parity mapping-torus convention represented by $Y_z=S^4\times S^1$ with pulled-back gauge connection and periodic spinors around $S^1$. Equivalently, a central $z$ gauge clutch combined with an antiperiodic spin clutch has this periodic total fermion boundary condition. A periodic spin clutch combined with the same $z$ gauge clutch would instead give antiperiodic total fermions; the two conventions must not be conflated in an eta-holonomy formula. For $N\ge1$ independent identical Weyl doublets, the local polynomial vanishes and the boundary holonomy on this loop is $(-1)^N$. Adopt, for this test, a five-dimensional invertible bulk response with phase $Z_{\mathrm{bulk}}(Y_z,A)=(-1)^{N\operatorname{ind}_2D_{Y_z}}$, where $\operatorname{ind}_2D_{Y_z}=\dim_{\mathbb R}\ker D_{Y_z}\bmod2$ for the real Dirac realization; then the bulk phase is $(-1)^N$ and the combined boundary/bulk holonomy is $+1$. For the finite normalization check take $K$ to be a single-vertex ordered simplicial complex and the ordinary field groupoid $\mathcal F(K)=BC_2$, with one object and automorphism group $C_2=\{1,z\}$. The boundary line alone has no invariant scalar gauging weight when $N$ is odd, while the boundary line tensored with the inverse bulk line has the normalized finite groupoid sum $1/2$. Even $N$ cancels this tested anomaly; this statement does not exclude other global or local anomalies outside the stated model and loop.

A $d$-dimensional boundary theory is **relative to an invertible bulk theory** when its partition value is a vector $Z_\partial(M,b|_M)$ in a specified one-dimensional Hermitian line $\mathcal L_\partial(M,b|_M)$, and the bulk assigns the dual line $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk}}(M,b|_M)\cong\mathcal L_\partial(M,b|_M)^*$ together with a vector $Z_{\mathrm{bulk}}(Y,b)$ in that line. The canonical evaluation

$$\mathrm{ev}:\mathcal L_\partial(M,b|_M)\otimes\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk}}(M,b|_M)\longrightarrow\mathbb C$$

then defines the combined scalar amplitude. Invertibility means that the bulk assigns a one-dimensional line to each closed $d$-dimensional boundary background and an isomorphism to each bordism map; orientation reversal replaces the assigned line by its dual. For a loop $\gamma$ of compatible background fields and endpoint gauge identifications, the boundary/bulk pair cancels that anomaly along $\gamma$ exactly when

$$\operatorname{Hol}_{\gamma}(\mathcal L_\partial)\operatorname{Hol}_{\gamma}(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk}})=1.$$

The diagram records this condition: the vertical maps are the line evaluation at the two endpoints, and the top map is parallel transport on both lines.

~~~tikzcd
\mathcal L_{\partial,0}\otimes\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk},0}
  \arrow[r,"\mathrm{PT}^{\partial}_{\gamma}\otimes\mathrm{PT}^{\mathrm{bulk}}_{\gamma}"]
  \arrow[d,"\mathrm{ev}_0"'] &
\mathcal L_{\partial,1}\otimes\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk},1}
  \arrow[d,"\mathrm{ev}_1"] \\
\mathbb C \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}_{\mathbb C}"'] & \mathbb C
~~~

A **finite groupoid** is a small category in which every morphism is invertible, with finitely many isomorphism classes and a finite automorphism group at every object. Write $\pi_0(\mathcal C)$ for its set of isomorphism classes. Its **groupoid cardinality** is

$$|\mathcal C|:=\sum_{[c]\in\pi_0(\mathcal C)}\frac{1}{|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal C}(c)|}.$$

For an isomorphism-invariant function $f:\pi_0(\mathcal C)\to\mathbb C$, define

$$\int_{c\in\mathcal C} f(c):=\sum_{[c]\in\pi_0(\mathcal C)}\frac{f(c)}{|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal C}(c)|}.$$

For finite groupoids $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$, a functor $p:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, and an object $d$ of $\mathcal D$, its **homotopy fiber** $\mathcal C_d$ has objects $(c,\alpha)$ with $\alpha:p(c)\overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow}d$ and morphisms $u:(c,\alpha)\to(c',\alpha')$ satisfying $\alpha'\circ p(u)=\alpha$. Define pullback and pushforward of invariant functions by

$$(p^*g)([c])=g([p(c)]),\qquad (p_!f)([d])=\int_{(c,\alpha)\in\mathcal C_d} f([c]).$$

A span $\mathcal X\xleftarrow{a}\mathcal E\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal Y$ of finite groupoids therefore induces the linear map $b_!a^*$ on invariant functions.

Assume full AC. Give the unit sphere $S^4\subset\mathbb R^5$ its boundary orientation, round metric and standard spin structure induced from the Euclidean ball. Let $S=S^+\oplus S^-$ be its complex spinor bundle, with skew-Hermitian Clifford action $c(v)c(w)+c(w)c(v)=-2\langle v,w\rangle$ and positive chirality the $+1$ eigenspace of $\Gamma=-c(e_1)c(e_2)c(e_3)c(e_4)$ in an oriented orthonormal frame. A spin lift here is a principal $\operatorname{Spin}(4)$ bundle double-covering the oriented orthonormal frame bundle; explicitly $\operatorname{Spin}(4)=Sp(1)\times Sp(1)$ covers $SO(4)$ by $(a,b):q\mapsto aqb^{-1}$ on $\mathbb H\cong\mathbb R^4$, where $Sp(1)$ is the unit-quaternion group, identified with $SU(2)$. The connection on spinors is the lift of the Levi-Civita connection. Set $E=S^+$ with its rank-two Hermitian $SU(2)$ connection $A_+$.

The twisted chiral Dirac operator $D^+_{A_+}=\sum_i c(e_i)\nabla_{e_i}:H^1(S^4;S^+\otimes E)\to L^2(S^4;S^-\otimes E)$ is Fredholm, with complex kernel dimension $1$, cokernel dimension $0$ and index $1$. In the anti-Hermitian Chern convention,

$$
\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle=\frac1{8\pi^2}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}(F_{A_+}\wedge F_{A_+})=-1.
$$

Its positive trace-form instanton charge $q=-(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int\operatorname{tr}(F\wedge F)$ is $1$; its connection is the scale-one self-dual BPST connection. More precisely there are parallel unitary identifications $F:\Lambda^0_{\mathbb C}\oplus\Lambda^2_{+,\mathbb C}\to S^+\otimes S^+$ and $G:\Lambda^1_{\mathbb C}\to S^-\otimes S^+$ under which

$$
G^{-1}D^+_{A_+}F(f,\omega)=df+\sqrt2\,d^*\omega.
$$

Here $\Lambda^2_+$ is the $+1$ Hodge-star subbundle, $d^*$ is the Riemannian formal adjoint, and all Sobolev spaces and adjoints use the specified bundle metrics. In the complete twisted spinor bundle the full Dirac operator is selfadjoint with domain $H^1$ and its square has domain $H^2$. This is a direct operator calculation for this explicit bundle, not an application of a general index formula.

Assume full AC and use the explicit round spin sphere, $E=S^+$ connection, Clifford action and chiral Dirac operator of the round-sphere spin-twist lemma. Let $Y=S^4\times(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)$ have product metric, pulled-back gauge connection and periodic, nonbounding circle spin structure. On the pulled-back complex bundle $S\otimes E$, put $c_5=i\Gamma$ and $D_5=D_4+i\Gamma\partial_t$, with periodic Sobolev domain $H^1$. There is a parallel antiunitary involution $J$ preserving $\ker D_5$, and the real skew-adjoint realization $iD_5$ on its $J$-fixed Hilbert space has

$$
\dim_{\mathbb R}(\ker D_5)^J=\dim_{\mathbb C}\ker D_4=1, \qquad \operatorname{ind}_2(iD_5):=\dim_{\mathbb R}(\ker D_5)^J\bmod2=1.
$$

More generally, let a nonempty compact closed oriented Riemannian spin four-manifold have a smooth unitary $SU(2)$ rank-two twist and a Fredholm chiral Dirac realization with $n_+=\dim_{\mathbb C}\ker D^+$ and $n_-=\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{coker}D^+$. With the same Clifford and periodic product conventions, the real product kernel has dimension $n_++n_-$, its parity is $\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb C}D^+\bmod2$, and the central action on its inverse determinant line is $(-1)^{\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb C}D^+}$. This general product statement does not assign an index value to an arbitrary bundle.

Let $z=-I$ be the central gauge automorphism of $E$. On the inverse chiral determinant line

$$
\mathcal L=(\det_{\mathbb C}\ker D^+)^*\otimes\det_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{coker}D^+
$$

its induced action is $-1$. For the constant connection path closed by $z$, the closed-loop automorphism $z_*^{-1}\circ\mathrm{PT}$ is $-1$ for any supplied connection on the determinant line. The $N$-fold tensor power has action $(-1)^N$.

The spin convention is part of the statement: using antiperiodic spinors in the circle direction gives no product zero mode. Equivalently, gluing the gauge fibers by $z=-1$ with an antiperiodic spin clutch gives periodic total spinor boundary conditions; gluing by $z$ with periodic spin clutch gives antiperiodic total boundary conditions instead. This distinguishes the tested fermion-parity mapping-torus convention from an automatic eta-holonomy formula. No general spectral-flow or Atiyah–Singer theorem is asserted.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.
